Stop opta-latest uploads deleting before they replace (#168)

* Lock pre-match predictions (#156); fix Projected goal-difference sign (#155)

Played games kept showing the latest model odds rather than the pre-match ones,
so 'called it / missed it' could not be shown. The lock writes a separate
predictions-locked.parquet by match day.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011vaJYTN3DQEVnfnLX83KyD

* build-blog-data: publish per-match team xG per league (team-match-xg-<code>.parquet)

The league-xg step already builds per-match, per-team xG for/against
(tmx) and only kept the season sum. Writing tmx per league gives the
inthegame-blog team page a rolling xG for/against chart without the 54 MB
match-shots file: ~190 KB for ENG, every season from 2011-12. Uploaded by
the existing blog/*.parquet R2 step; nothing else changes.

Checked locally on the live R2 inputs: 8,739 ENG rows, 191,059 bytes,
values match a pandas rebuild (Arsenal 2026-27 1.48/0.28, 1.30/0.26 ...).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_017AcywyoortCWgu9DMUxD4f

* team-match-xg: write after league-xg.parquet (review)

A failure in the new per-league loop can no longer stop league-xg.parquet.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_017AcywyoortCWgu9DMUxD4f

* build-blog-data: write predictions-recent.parquet (last 450 days) beside the full file

The blog's football hub, matches and match pages read all 59,613 prediction
rows (48 seasons, 2.4 MB) to show recent weeks. The recent file is 8,372
rows / 358 KB (checked locally on the live file). Full file unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_017AcywyoortCWgu9DMUxD4f

* Strip oversized R metadata from blog parquets before upload

arrow's write_parquet stores a data frame's R attributes in the footer, and a
grouped frame stores every row index there. On 2026-10-06 the blog's
football/shots.parquet was 39.8 MB with a 37.6 MB footer (2.2 MB of shots),
match-shots 54.5 MB (37.6 MB footer), afl/game-stats 10.4 MB (8.8 MB footer),
player-positions 3.4 MB (1.5 MB footer). Browsers download the whole footer
before any data and never use R attributes.

scripts/strip_parquet_r_metadata.R rewrites only files whose footer is over
1 MB, keeping row-group size; tested on copies of all four live files: data
identical, footers 4-40 KB, a second run changes nothing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_017AcywyoortCWgu9DMUxD4f

* Re-score stored direct corners at panna's fixed xG / xGOT

panna#278 scores direct-from-corner shots at xG 0.02 and on-target xGOT
0.08, but the daily scorer only fills shots with no stored value, so the
~330 already-scored direct corners would keep the model's ~0.85. Any
stored direct corner whose value is not the constant is now re-scored;
once fixed it drops out. Checked on EPL 2023-2024: 1 of 10,538 rows
changed (Ward-Prowse 0.199 -> 0.02, xGOT 0.996 -> 0.08), second run
re-scores nothing.

Refs peteowen1/panna#277

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_017B5tG6Sf6CQGeMbVK3gV4H

* Set stored direct corners to the constant instead of re-scoring them

Review of 51b19e0 found a daily loop: a blocked direct corner gets xGOT 0
from panna, never 0.08, and a direct corner with no event context keeps its
stored value, so both were re-selected every run, defeating the early exit
and rewriting the whole shot file daily. The value is a constant, so set it
directly on stored rows (blocked shots left alone). Checked on all 340
corner-flag rows plus EPL 2023-2024: run 1 set 340 xG / 294 xGOT, nothing
outside the box changed, the 6 blocked rows kept their values, run 2 did
nothing.

Refs peteowen1/panna#277

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_017B5tG6Sf6CQGeMbVK3gV4H

* Per-player and per-team copies of match-stats and game-logs, plus a player index (pannadata#164)

/football/player read whole match-stats-<CODE> (103,323 rows for GER) and
game-logs files to keep one player's rows, and waited on the full
ratings.parquet to learn the player's name and league. /football/team read
the whole match-stats shard (124,548 rows for ENG) for one club.

scripts/by_player.R writes sibling files after the originals:
- match-stats-<CODE>-by-player and game-logs-by-player: sorted by player_id,
  row groups of up to 1,500 rows that never split a player, so a player_id
  filter reads one group.
- match-stats-<CODE>-by-team: one row group per club, both teams' rows of
  each match the club played, with for_team; checked 2x the original's rows
  and groups = clubs.
- player-index (from build_blog_data.R, same rows as ratings.parquet, checked).
The originals are not re-sorted: /football/match reads them by match. Every
copy is optional: a failure warns and the page falls back.

Checked on all 17 live match-stats shards and game-logs from R2: 34 of 34
copies written, row counts equal (by-team = 2x), every player in one group.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_017B5tG6Sf6CQGeMbVK3gV4H

* by_player.R: pack clubs and players into 5,000-row groups, key-only statistics, footer guard

Review finding: one row group per club gave match-stats-UEL-by-team 376
groups and a 1.5 MB footer (UECL 1.2 MB). A browser downloads the whole
footer before any row, and strip_parquet_r_metadata.R rewrites any file
with a footer over 1 MB, re-chunking it at an arbitrary size and losing the
one-club-per-group layout.

Now small clubs share a group (no club is split), groups hold up to 5,000
rows (footer plus one group was smallest there on ENG/ENG2/UEL; 1,500 rows
gave ENG2 a 431 KB footer to read a 63 KB group), min/max statistics are
written for the filter key only, and the writer stops if a footer passes
900 KB. Re-run on all 17 live shards and game-logs: 35 of 35 written,
footers 10-135 KB, no key split across groups, strip step rewrites none.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_017B5tG6Sf6CQGeMbVK3gV4H

* By-player writer: drop R attribute metadata before writing

The 2026-10-07 torpdata build wrote game-stats-by-player.parquet with an
8.7 MB footer (R attributes under the footer key "r"). The strip step then
rewrote it at a fixed group size, leaving 18 of 1,122 players across two
row groups on R2. Dropping the key in the writer, as the strip step does,
keeps the footer small so the strip step leaves the file alone. Not
reproduced locally (the published input was already stripped); the CI
strip took that file's footer from 8.9 MB to 124 KB by removing this key.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_017B5tG6Sf6CQGeMbVK3gV4H

* Daily scrape: load panna R/ at 9dfa1b9 so the scorer finds .is_direct_corner()

score_shots_context.R loads six panna R/ files at PANNA_REF. The pin was
81e23c2 (panna#271), which predates .is_direct_corner() (panna#277/#278).
Since 51f5501 called it, the 2026-10-06 scrape died with "could not find
function .is_direct_corner": no direct corner got its fixed value
(inthegame-blog: all 15 corner-flag shots unchanged on R2) and that day's
new shots shipped with no xG. The step only echoes ::error::, so the run
stayed green. 2026-10-05 and earlier scored normally.

commits (additions). Smoke-tested: the six files load from GitHub at
9dfa1b9, .is_direct_corner() exists, and it matches the 15 rows.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_017B5tG6Sf6CQGeMbVK3gV4H

* Stop opta-latest uploads deleting before they replace

`gh release upload --clobber` deletes the existing asset first, so an
upload that then fails leaves the release without it (wheather lost its
cache this way on 2026-09-17). For opta-latest that is worse than a
missing file: the restore steps swallowed download failures, the scraper
reads a missing manifest as "first run", and the next upload would put a
cut-down file over the whole history.

- versebus.sh 1.3.0: vb_sh_safe_upload uploads under a temp name,
  waits for state "uploaded" at the local size, then deletes the old
  asset and renames. vb_sh_restore downloads with a size check, falls
  back to a stranded temp copy, and returns 1 (failed) vs 2 (absent) so
  a transient error can't read as absence. vb_sh_upload_all and
  vb_sh_manifest_last use them, which also covers panna's
  epv-pipeline.yml (it fetches this file from main).
- daily-opta-scrape.yml: one restore step that refuses to scrape when a
  listed file fails to download, or when a core file or an events file
  the previous bus_manifest.json names is missing (override:
  allow_missing_assets). Every --clobber upload is now a safe upload.
- rebuild-events.yml: the prior events file and the event-less registry
  no longer `|| true` past a download failure.
- build-tournament-timing.yml: safe upload.
- test_versebus.sh: a stateful fake release; new cases for each failure
  point of the swap and every restore return code, plus a guard that no
  workflow uploads with --clobber. 59/59 pass locally.

Audit: vault/plans/CLOBBER-AUDIT-2026-10-08.md (items 1-2 of 7 HIGH).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01KBeYbYqubvjN1CZarLmAAX

* Fix the opta-latest restore failing on the live release

The dev dry run (run 37742543338) failed at the new restore step: the
exported asset listing was 221 KB (GitHub attaches an uploader object to
every asset), over Linux's 128 KB limit for one environment string, so
every later exec died with "Argument list too long". Worse, vb_sh_restore
read jq's empty output as "absent" and reported a present
bus_manifest.json as missing -- the exact error-read-as-absence this
change exists to remove.

- vb_sh_list_assets trims the listing to id/name/size/state/created_at
  (16.7 KB for opta-latest's 134 assets); the workflow no longer exports it.
- vb_sh_restore returns 1 on any jq failure, never 2.
- vb_sh_safe_upload: a jq failure can only keep the old asset.
- Tests: jq-failure and field-trim cases. 61/61 pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01KBeYbYqubvjN1CZarLmAAX

* Address review: set -e callers, half uploads, lost rebuild priors

- vb_sh_upload_all always returns 0. It ended on the last file's status,
  so panna's `out=$(vb_sh_upload_all ...)` under `set -euo pipefail`
  would die on a failing last upload before reading the FAIL lines --
  killing the ~2h EPV job that step is meant to soft-fail through.
- vb_sh_restore returns 1, not 2, for an asset listed under its real
  name but not in state "uploaded" (a killed upload is broken, not absent).
- rebuild-events.yml: a missing prior events_<comp>.parquet or event-less
  registry now fails unless the dispatch sets allow_missing_prior=true.
  A lost file looked exactly like a new competition, and the upload
  would have replaced the history with one season.
- Tests: set -e caller and half-upload cases (both fail on the old
  code). 63/63 pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01KBeYbYqubvjN1CZarLmAAX
